provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: Original family: an odd n x n grid has a block of random colours (never 0 or 5) above a full line of colour 5. Everything below that line is 0. The output writes the block's unique most frequent colour into the bottom row at the centre column. Under D4, the block's side is determined only by the rotation count, because a horizontal mirror leaves the top side on top and keeps the odd centre column fixed. Each clockwise rotation moves the side top -> right -> bottom -> left. The factory therefore specialises two things: the block side, and the divider colour palette[5]. The emitted program works in visible coordinates. It finds the divider line, which is a row or column of palette[5], scanning on the axis that matches the side. As a fallback it takes the first uniform line, then the middle line. It tallies the colours in the block on the specialised side, takes the most frequent one (ties go to the smallest value, but the generator guarantees a unique maximum), and writes it at the centre of the grid edge opposite the block.
draft_notes.limitations: Assumes the constructor's domain: odd square grids with exactly one full divider line of palette[5], and block colours that exclude palette[5]. For rectangular grids it still uses (len-1)//2 as the centre along the target edge, but that case is outside the generator's domain. No tests were run. The fixtures are consistent with the uniform rule.
